planting.note: Set divisions out in spring once soil is workable, spacing them to allow the mounding clump room to fill in over a season or two.

directions: This Heucherella villosa hybrid forms a dense mound of lime-green leaves marked with flame-shaped cherry-red centers that deepen to mahogany as the season progresses. It handles heat and humidity better than many Heucherella selections and sends up airy stems of small cream flowers in late spring. Grow it in humus-rich, evenly moist soil with afternoon shade, dividing congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich soil with afternoon shade, where leaf color develops most intensely.

directions: Copper King produces large, deeply dissected, maple-like leaves roughly 5 inches across in bright orange with copper-red centers and yellow edging, holding color best with some afternoon shade. White flowers rise on red stems in late spring on scapes well above the foliage, drawing in bees. It is an evergreen groundcover in milder climates and benefits from a periodic spring division once the clump becomes crowded.

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring into acidic to neutral, humus-rich soil, keeping the crown consistently moist while new fronds establish.

directions: This selection carries the typical silver-and-green coloring of Japanese painted fern but adds double-crested, frilled tips to each frond for extra textural interest. It spreads at a medium rate into an architectural clump well suited to woodland borders and shaded containers. Keep soil consistently moist with slightly acidic to neutral pH, and it is generally left alone by deer and rabbits.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in rich, constantly moist soil, ideally at a pond edge or boggy spot, with protection from hot afternoon sun.

directions: Big Green Tractor is a bold-foliage ligularia (a cross of L. japonica and L. dentata) with massive, deeply serrated, glossy green leaves that reach about 16 inches across at maturity. Branched spikes of golden-yellow, daisy-like flowers with long petals open in midsummer, though flowering is reduced in deeper shade. It needs a steady supply of moisture and performs best with afternoon shade, making it a natural fit for pond margins and consistently damp borders.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, evenly moist soil in shade; some morning sun can intensify leaf color without the scorch risk of afternoon exposure.

directions: Time in a Bottle forms a low, wide mound of narrow, moderately wavy leaves that open yellow and shift toward chartreuse as the season progresses. Deep purple flowers appear on scapes in late summer but stay mostly closed, extending their display time compared with typical open hosta blooms. Grow it in average to fertile, consistently moist soil in part to full shade, and divide crowded clumps in spring as needed.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, well-drained, highly organic soil in part to full shade, giving this large-spreading hosta plenty of room to fill out.

directions: Drop-dead Gorgeous is a large, vigorous hosta (Empress Wu x Niagara Falls) with broad, ovate leaves that have green centers framed by brightly contrasting, heavily rippled yellow margins, creating a lightly wavy overall look. White flowers appear on tall scapes in midsummer and attract butterflies. It spreads quickly into a substantial specimen clump, so give it generous room in a woodland or shade border with consistently moist, humus-rich soil.
